messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: High CPU and OOMs observed on inference-tokenizer pods in us-west-2 cluster. Auto-paged @oncall. Rule: tokenizer.cpu > 85% for 3m, pod restarts detected.
Sam C.: I’m on it — pulling logs now. Which deployment?
Jordan L.: looks like `tokenizer-preproc-v2` replicas in namespace `inference-prod` — several in CrashLoopBackOff with `OOMKilled`.
Priya M.: seeing a lot of identical requests with huge prompt lengths from a single customer IP range, possible thundering-herd of heavy prompts.
Alex G.: confirming, metrics show 7x normal 99th percentile token length between 02:12–02:18 UTC.
Sam C.: grabbing one pod log: ```stderr
2026-03-15T02:16:03Z ERROR TokenizerWorker: memory spike, attempting alloc 512MB
RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory
Killed
```
Sam C.: pod shows OOMKilled then node wrapped with `kubelet: evict` messages.
Jordan L.: can we temporarily scale down tokenization concurrency? There is an env `MAX_TOKENIZER_WORKERS`. Set to 2 for now.
Priya M.: on it — patching deployment with `kubectl set env deploy/tokenizer-preproc-v2 MAX_TOKENIZER_WORKERS=2 -n inference-prod` and bumping restart to force rolling update.
ops-bot: Command executed: `kubectl set env deploy/tokenizer-preproc-v2 MAX_TOKENIZER_WORKERS=2 -n inference-prod` by Priya M. (ok).
Alex G.: traffic router is still sending to same pool. Propose enabling routing fallback to `tokenizer-lite` for requests with prompt len > 8k. Can we flip that safely?
Sam C.: yes, but need to register a temporary policy in routing: `route: if prompt_len > 8000 -> tokenizer-lite` — I'll open a quick rollbackable flag.
SRE Pager: please collect `kubectl top pods -n inference-prod` and `kubectl describe node <node>` for the affected nodes. Might be node-level memory pressure.
Sam C.: `kubectl top pods` shows tokenizer pods at 1200Mi vs request 256Mi (bad). Node memory 95% used. Suspect runaway concurrency ignoring cgroups.
Jordan L.: creating a temporary HPA pod eviction: cordon one noisy node, drain non-critical pods. `kubectl cordon node/ip-10-2-5-14` and `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` — doing it now.
Priya M.: cordon/drain executed. Old pods evicted and restarted on healthier nodes. Seeing fewer OOMs already.
Alex G.: routing fallback enabled, tokenization concurrency env patched. We should also enforce `requests/limits` on the tokenizer container; a quick patch to set limit memory=512Mi.
Sam C.: applied memory limit to deployment (limit 512Mi). Rolling restart in progress.
ops-bot: Deployment `tokenizer-preproc-v2` updated by Sam C. — rollout 3/5 pods ready.
Priya M.: monitoring logs for CUDA errors after restart. Early signs look better. No new OOMKilled events in last 2 minutes.
Jordan L.: checking customer impact — cross-referencing error logs with customer IDs. Looks like 4 customers saw increased error rates (5xx) during the spike. Not seeing widespread impact to embeddings/other services.
Sam C.: posting to status page: https://status.internal.redwood.com/incidents/2112345678 — noting degraded tokenization for some customers between 02:12-02:22 UTC.
Alex G.: recommending longer-term fix: enforce request size gating at API gateway, prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, and add a circuit-breaker that demotes huge prompts to a batch queue.
SRE Pager: agree. Also open a post-incident to add better cgroup enforcement and to ensure tokenizer honors `MAX_TOKENIZER_WORKERS`.
Priya M.: handoff — I’ll run until 03:00 UTC then pass to oncall for overlap. No known customer-visible regressions remaining.
Sam C.: taking handoff at 03:00 UTC. Leaving notes: changed env MAX_TOKENIZER_WORKERS=2, memory limit 512Mi, routing fallback on, cordoned node ip-10-2-5-14.
Jordan L.: ticket filed: INF-4872 "Tokenizer: enforce resource limits and add prompt-size gating" with remediation steps and metrics.
Alex G.: quick follow-up: we should also throttle requests from offending IP range at the edge for 1 hour. I added rule to WAF: `block 203.0.113.0/24` (temporary).
Priya M.: confirmed blocked.
ops-bot: Note: automated rollback disabled for this deployment for 30m to avoid flip-flopping.
Sam C.: good catches everyone. I’ll keep watching dashboards for 30m. If we see repeat, escalate to infra lead.
Priya M.: :thumbsup: closing active pager. Will write up RCA and list customers to notify.
incident-bot: Pager resolved by Sam C. at 03:10 UTC. Incident state -> mitigated.
SRE Pager: leaving on-call note: please follow up on root cause (tokenizer memory accounting bug) in the postmortem.
Sam C.: saving logs + traces to infra bucket s3://redwood-incident-logs/2112345678/*. Also will attach a small script to reproduce heavy prompt pattern for QA.
Jordan L.: rough ETA for postmortem draft 24h. Assigning owners: Jordan (technical), Priya (customer comms).
Priya M.: will reach out to affected customers with timeline and mitigation actions.
SRE Pager: handoff complete. If anyone sees reappearance, re-open pager.
